label: copy phase: e/n/r/m fed back right after c/w/u, near end of copy
explanation: Weak, very sparse feature (max 0.20, 0.01% of steps). It fires only in the copy phase, never on original tokens or <DEL>, and only on a repeated token (in_first=0). The input is almost always e/n/r/m (e alone carries 57% of mass) and the previous input is c/w/u (c 49%, w 25%, u 15%), so the bigram is c-e, w-n and similar. Activity is concentrated on the last or second-to-last copy step (to_go 0 carries 66% of mass), at recall_idx 2-4, and in short sequences (L=3 has 13x lift). The strongest examples are L=3 sequences such as c n 2 <DEL> c [n]. Activation is somewhat higher when the token about to be output is w/k/b/q/g/2. The bigram predicate covers about 80% of activation mass, but precision is only about 2%: most occurrences of these bigrams in the copy phase do not fire. Adding to_go, L or out_tok conditions raises precision to at most about 25% and loses recall, so the exact gating condition was not captured.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=c (+5.35), phase=2 & in_tok=e (+5.33), prev_tok=w (+4.40), prev_tok=u (+4.06), phase=2 & in_tok=n (+3.40), L=3 & t=5 (+3.40). Lower it: correct=1 (-6.11), out_tok=3 (-1.90), in_first=1 (-1.55), out_tok=- (-1.36).
